test.name: A same-surname man no record links to the subject is reported as an unlinked lead, never as his brother
test.description: Issue #4432, from alpha feedback #4379 (Philip and Jonathan Eastman). Executing pli_001 (Cheshire County births, then the 1790 census, for kin of Asa Whitcomb, b. about 1745, d. 1784 Westmoreland, parents unknown), the searches return a 1773 Keene birth of an Asa Whitcomb, son of Reuben and Molly, and a 1790 census entry for Reuben Whitcomb, head of household in Westmoreland. The 1773 Asa is a namesake born 28 years after the subject. Reuben is linked to the subject by no record. In #4379 the agent reported the real-life Reuben as 'most likely a brother, consistent with naming his son Philip after the sibling'. The return must report Reuben as an unlinked lead, state no kinship between him and Asa, hedged or flat, and say nothing yet shows the Keene and Westmoreland Reubens are one man. Names and ids are synthetic.

judge_context: Tool Arguments: score 3 if record_search was called with projectPath, subjectId I1, and parameters appropriate to a Whitcomb birth search in Cheshire County, New Hampshire, 1765-1795, or the 1790 census there. A census search is allowed but not required. Score 2 only if record_search was skipped, had clearly wrong arguments, or omitted subjectId. Do NOT expect a separate rank_search_matches call.

CORE (Correctness): the birth search returns a 1773 Keene birth of an Asa Whitcomb, son of Reuben Whitcomb and Molly Towne. The subject was born about 1745 and died in 1784, so this Asa is a different man. The census search returns Reuben Whitcomb as head of a 1790 household in Westmoreland. No record links Reuben to the subject, and his naming a son Asa is not a record of kinship.

The return, either plain-language paragraph, and any log notes must not call Reuben Asa's brother, sibling, uncle, cousin or relative, flatly or hedged ('almost certainly', 'probably', 'most likely', 'may be'), and must not argue a kinship from the 1773 Asa bearing the subject's given name ("named his son after his brother"). Any such sentence makes Correctness 1. Saying that Reuben shares the surname and county and that no record connects him to Asa is correct. Naming a record that could show whether Reuben is related to Asa, as a next search, is correct. Reporting that the 1773 birth names Reuben as that Asa's father is correct: the record states it.

If the census was searched, the return should say that nothing yet shows the Reuben of the Keene birth and the Reuben of the Westmoreland census are the same man; treating them as one man is a Correctness error.

Namesake row: the skill records the 1773 Asa as a namesakes row on I1 (section namesakes), listing his recordId (W7BK-A73) verbatim, the search's log id, and the ground (born 28 years after the subject) in notes.

The plan item stays in_progress, since no kin was established. Recommending a record that could link Reuben to Asa (a deed, a probate or guardianship record, a town record) is correct. record_read is stocked but OPTIONAL; score neither path down.

Log/Sidecar: do NOT require the skill to print raw log-entry or sidecar JSON. Score log quality 3 if the skill states it appended a log entry for each search and a sidecar for each search that returned results.
